claim: When a device or media handle is acquired asynchronously (a camera or mic grant behind a permission prompt), give the effect that asked a liveness flag and stop a handle that arrives after it was released, because the consumer can let go while the prompt is open and the late grant is otherwise kept with nobody to reap it.
because: phone camera effect: a grant landing after the panel changed became the active camera; red then green. media-resource-lifecycle covers reap-on-replace and unmount but not the in-flight acquisition race.

claim: When a test claims work runs concurrently, assert how many units were in flight at once (or release the stubs only when all have started), never an elapsed-time upper bound, because a loaded runner stretches every timer and turns a concurrency claim into a race against the machine.
because: a parallel-health suite case (<120 ms over four 40 ms stubs) failed 52 of 64 runs under parallel load; an in-flight count failed 0 of 64 and still caught a deliberately serial version (peak 1).

claim: When commands (not state) cross from I/O threads into a UI loop, carry them on a queue, not a latest-value holder, because a latest-value holder silently drops every command of a burst but the last.
because: undo/redo/seek were sent through a latest-value flow read by recomposition; a test showed 1 of 3 back-to-back commands delivered, and a channel fixed it to 3 of 3.

claim: When a gate starts a tool through the package manager's shim directory (node_modules/.bin and the like) and the install may be a link to another checkout, start the tool by its package file instead, because the shims are not part of the linked packages and an 'is it installed' check over the packages passes while the shim lookup fails.
because: in every worktree the preflight checked the compiler's package through a junction and passed, then the gate failed with 'not recognized' because the donor install had no shim directory; starting the compiler by its file took the typecheck gate from exit 1 to exit 0 with no write to the donor.

claim: When focus is model-driven (a D-pad or remote moves a state index and the element only carries a data-focused or CSS ring, while DOM focus stays on one container), have the view-model produce the spoken line for the lit stop and render it in one polite, atomic live region per surface, because the focus ring never reaches the accessibility tree and nothing else tells a screen reader what Select will open.
because: the TV landing had DOM focus parked on the stage (tabIndex=0) and its lit stop only in data-focused/data-lit; adding view.say in an aria-live region made the region's text follow data-lit in a real browser (phone -> Essay Master -> Linga), with the repo's live check (type floor, safe zone) still green.

claim: When a gate borrows a dependency install from another checkout (a link to a donor node_modules), take donors only from the version-control system's own worktree list or an explicit variable, never from a directory crawl up the tree, because the donor's code runs inside the gate and crawled parents include directories every local user can write (shared profile folders, the drive root, /tmp).
because: a worktree preflight crawled 3 parent levels and on a real machine reached C:\Users\Public (interactive users: modify) and 37 drive-root folders (authenticated users may create folders); restricting to git worktree list cut the default to 11 candidates, all worktrees of the repo, with the suite green.
